# Aunt Jamesina

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052)</sub>
- **Role:** housekeeper  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- **Titles:** queen of housemothers  <sub>[v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Aunt Jimsie  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>

## Appearance

Aunt Jamesina is a tiny old woman with a softly-triangular face, pink cheeks, and snow-white hair worn in quaint little puffs over her ears. She has large, soft blue eyes filled with youth, hope, and a mirthful twinkle. She wears old-fashioned clothes.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c18 P2](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0002)_

## Personality

Aunt Jamesina is sweet, cheerful, and holds old-fashioned opinions, though she is relaxed about enforcing proper behavior on young people. She possesses a philosophy of doing her duty to God, her neighbor, and herself while enjoying life. She has a playful streak, having made fun of her suitors in her youth, yet maintains a deep respect for the clergy. Though she loves the young women under her care deeply, she admits she does not always fully understand them.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c19 P4](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0004), [v3 c19 P40](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0040), [v3 c24 P5](../source/v03-c24.md#nw-v03-c24-p0005), [v3 c35 P21](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0021), [v3 c37 P42](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0042)_

## History

Aunt Jamesina was named after her father James, who drowned at sea a month before she was born. In her youth, she desired a yellow silk dress, but neither her mother nor her husband permitted her to have one. She raised a daughter named Elizabeth, whom she taught to cook before she attended college; Elizabeth eventually married and went to India as a foreign missionary, a path Aunt Jamesina had prayed for despite worrying about the snakes there. Left alone in a large house, Aunt Jamesina accepted an invitation to move to Kingsport to keep house for a group of college students—including Anne Shirley, Stella, Priscilla, and Phil Gordon—at Patty's Place. She brought along her grey-and-white cat, the Sarah-cat, and took charge of the household and its pets, including Joseph and Rusty. Over three college winters, she served as a beloved housemother to the young women. At the end of their studies, she decided to take Rusty home with her alongside Joseph and the Sarah-cat.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P23](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0023), [v3 c16 P58](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0058), [v3 c18 P25](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0025), [v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006), [v3 c27 P6](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0006), [v3 c36 P11](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0011), [v3 c37 P12](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0012), [v3 c38 P8](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0008)_

## Quotes

> New shoes are smarter than old ones, but the old ones are more comfortable. I’m old enough to indulge myself in the matter of shoes and opinions. I mean to take it real easy here. I know you expect me to look after you and keep you proper, but I’m not going to do it. You’re old enough to know how to behave if you’re ever going to be. So, as far as I am concerned, you can all go to destruction in your own way.  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>

> Do your duty by God and your neighbor and yourself, and have a good time. That’s my philosophy and it’s always worked pretty well.  <sub>[v3 c19 P4](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0004)</sub>

> The very first thing I’m going to do when I get to heaven is to get a yellow silk dress.  <sub>[v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>

> I am not decrying the higher education of women. My daughter is an M.A. She can cook, too. But I taught her to cook before I let a college professor teach her Mathematics.  <sub>[v3 c27 P6](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0006)</sub>

> It isn’t in good taste to make fun of your beaux, but I always did it myself.  <sub>[v3 c35 P21](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0021)</sub>
